lighthouses.name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse
lighthouses.owner: National Park Service (tower); US Coast Guard (light)
history: The first tower on the cape was a sandstone light from 1802. The present brick tower was first lit on December 16, 1871.

Shoreline erosion threatened the tower for decades. The light moved to a steel skeleton tower in 1935 and came back to the brick tower in 1950. In 1999 the whole tower was moved 2,900 feet inland, a job finished on September 14, 1999.

lighthouses.name: Portland Head Light
lighthouses.owner: Town of Cape Elizabeth (grounds, museum); US Coast Guard (light)
history: Local masons began the tower in 1787 and it was first lit on January 10, 1791. The tower's height was raised and lowered several times in the 1800s before settling in 1885.
The light was automated in 1989, and the keeper's house is now a maritime museum run on the town-owned grounds.

lighthouses.name: Point Reyes Lighthouse
history: The short cast-iron tower was built in 1870 low on the headland, so its light sits 265 feet above the sea. It was automated in 1975.
Its first-order Fresnel lens went through a 15-month restoration finished in November 2019. The station was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1991.

lighthouses.name: Split Rock Lighthouse
lighthouses.place: Split Rock Lighthouse State Park, Two Harbors, Minnesota
history: The lighthouse was built after the 1905 Mataafa Storm wrecked or damaged many ships on Lake Superior, and it was first lit on July 31, 1910 on a cliff about 130 feet above the lake.
It was electrified in 1940, its fog signal stopped in 1961, and the Coast Guard retired the light in 1969. It is now a historic site and was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2011.

lighthouses.name: Ponce de Leon Inlet Light
lighthouses.owner: Town of Ponce Inlet; museum run by the Ponce de Leon Inlet Lighthouse Preservation Association
history: A first lighthouse went up on the inlet in 1835 but was never lit and collapsed the next year. The present 175-foot tower was finished and first lit in 1887.
The Coast Guard moved its beacon to New Smyrna Beach in 1970. High-rise buildings later blocked that beacon, so the old tower was relit in 1982 and now runs as a private aid to navigation.

lighthouses.name: Pigeon Point Lighthouse
lighthouses.owner: California State Parks; keeper housing run by HI USA
history: The point takes its name from the ship Carrier Pigeon, wrecked there in 1853. The tower was first lit at sunset on November 15, 1872.

It switched from lard oil to kerosene in 1888, to electricity in 1926, and was automated in 1974. Tours have been closed since 2001 because of corroded ironwork; a $16 million rehabilitation was announced in December 2023.

lighthouses.name: Heceta Head Light
lighthouses.owner: Oregon Parks and Recreation (light); US Forest Service (keeper's house)
history: Approved in 1888, the station was built in 1892–93 with materials brought in by ship and wagon, and the light was first lit in 1894. Its first-order Fresnel lens is by Chance Brothers.
The light was automated in 1963 and the last keepers left. The tower closed for restoration in 2011 and reopened on June 8, 2013.

stay.notes: Six rooms, open year-round, with a multi-course breakfast and an afternoon wine and cheese social.

lighthouses.name: Saugerties Lighthouse
history: The 1869 lighthouse replaced an earlier 1838 light on the Hudson River. Coast Guard service ended in 1954.
The nonprofit Saugerties Lighthouse Conservancy bought it in 1986 and restored it. It now holds a small museum and is on the National Register of Historic Places (1979).

stay.notes: River-view rooms with breakfast. Wikipedia lists two B&B rooms. The trail to the light can close at storm tides.

lighthouses.name: Big Bay Point Lighthouse
history: The lighthouse was built on a bluff over Lake Superior and its third-order lens entered service on October 20, 1896.
It was deactivated and sold in 1961 and passed through several private owners. It has operated as a bed and breakfast since 1986.

lighthouses.name: Rose Island Lighthouse
lighthouses.place: Rose Island, Narragansett Bay, Newport, Rhode Island
history: The lighthouse was built in 1870 on a bastion of the old Fort Hamilton. It was abandoned as a working light in 1970 once the Newport Bridge opened.
The Rose Island Lighthouse Foundation formed in 1984 to restore it, it joined the National Register in 1987, and it was relit as a private aid to navigation in 1992.

lighthouses.name: East Brother Island Light
lighthouses.place: East Brother Island, San Pablo Strait, Richmond, California
history: The station was built on a small island the government already owned, because land on the mainland was too costly. The lamp was first lit on March 1, 1874 and marks the entrance to San Pablo Bay.
It was automated in 1969 and listed on the National Register in 1971. A nonprofit formed in 1979 restored the buildings, and the keeper's house has run as a bed and breakfast since 1980.

stay.kind: Bed and breakfast on the island
stay.notes: Five rooms. Rates include the boat ride, a tour, a four-course dinner and breakfast. Book in advance.
